# UI style

Rules for everything visible in the window. New tools and buttons follow them.

## Icons

* SVG files in `assets/icons/`, drawn on a **24 x 24 grid** (`viewBox="0 0 24 24"`), generated by `scripts/gen_assets.py`.
* **One stroke width: 1.75 px**, round line caps and round joins, no fills except a light (30 %) fill of the accent shape.
* **Two colours only**: a neutral colour that follows the theme (token `#NEUTRAL`) and one accent colour (token `#ACCENT`).
  The application replaces the tokens when it loads an icon (dark theme: light grey and amber).
* The **accent marks the result of the operation** (the extruded part, the new line, the rounded corner, the selected face);
  everything that is context or the starting situation is neutral.
* Icons must be **illustrative first**: a small picture of what happens (a cube with its top face highlighted, an arrow
  that pulls a face up), not an abstract symbol. They must stay readable at 24 px; `icons-preview.html` shows them at 24 and 48 px.
* Keep 2 px of empty margin inside the grid, centre the drawing, avoid details thinner than the stroke.

## Tool buttons

* Left strip: icon (24 px) with the tool name next to it. Active tool: selected button state.
* Hovering a button for about half a second shows a **help card**: name, keyboard shortcut, a larger before/after
  illustration (`assets/help/<id>.svg`, 240 x 140), two or three sentences how to use it and optional tips.
* The content of the cards is data, not code: `assets/help/tools.json`, one record per tool
  (`id`, `title`, `shortcut`, `text`, `tips`, `illustration`, `animation`). `animation` is reserved for later animated
  demonstrations (a file name); it is `null` today and ignored by the viewer. Add or change a card by editing the data only.
* Help illustrations use the same two colour tokens, labelled "before" and "after", result in the accent colour.

## Tool bars

* **Top bar** (above the view): Sketch, Line, Rectangle, Circle, Arc, Move sketch plane with its Offset field, Plan view, 3D mode.
  New drawing-related tools (Sweep, helix, dimensions, ...) are added to this bar as further items of `toolbar_items()`; the bar
  adapts by itself: labels and icons while there is room, only icons in a narrower window, and what still does not fit goes under a
  "More" button (`layout_mode` in `app/toolbar.rs`, unit tested).
* **Left column**: Tools (Select, Pull, Move, Combine, Loft, Sweep, Measure, then Fill and Join ends as icons), Edges (Round, Chamfer) and Edit side by side, View, File, then Settings and About.
  It must fit a 1280 x 720 window without scrolling (the self test measures it at 1280 x 720 and 1920 x 1080 and saves screenshots); the
  status bar is declared before the side panels, so that they end above it. Rows are tight (2 px) and Edges/Edit and the four views are single rows.
* **File block**: a frame with a muted dark-yellow edge (`icons::file_frame_color`), large icon buttons (`icons::file_button`): 38 px icons in 3 columns
  when the middle part of the column leaves room for them, 32 px when there is less room, else 22 px in 4 columns (`file_block_layout`). The icons
  of the block are drawn with thin lines, about half of the usual width (`FILE_BLOCK_ICONS` in `scripts/gen_assets.py`: 0.9 instead of 1.75, the
  letters 1.0). The exchange icons draw the format name (STL, STEP) in block letters **below** the sheet, never inside it, with a margin to the
  edge of the icon (`exchange()`); the same icons are used wherever STL/STEP appear, so the letters are equally large everywhere.
* **The left column is split in two**: the middle part (Tools, Edges, Edit, View) scrolls with the mouse wheel when the window is lower than the
  column needs; the File block and the Settings / About buttons below it are fixed and always visible. The self test checks windows of
  1280 x 720, 1920 x 1080, 1280 x 600 and 1920 x 1080 at the scales 1.25 and 1.5 (from 720 points high nothing scrolls).
* **A button never disappears and never moves.** One that cannot be used in the current state keeps its white (black in the light theme) text and
  shows the state in its background, frame, dimmed icon and indicator; it does not react to clicks and its tooltip starts
  with the reason in amber (for example "Start a sketch first", "Select an edge first", "Combine needs at least two bodies"), followed by
  the help card. The reasons are decided in `toolbar_items()` and `left_column()`.
* The keyboard shortcut of a top bar button is a small letter in its lower right corner (also in icon-only mode) and part of the tooltip.
* Hovering a greyed-out button still shows the card; `icons::tool_button_why` / `icon_button_why` are the only way to draw these buttons.

## Floating panels

* Panels next to an object (Edges, face, dimensions, Move, Combine, Loft, Revolve) are drawn by `app/dock.rs`. Drag a panel by its
  title bar; a dashed line leads from the panel to the place it belongs to once it was moved away; it cannot leave the window; a double
  click on the title puts it back. The position is remembered per kind of panel until the program ends (not in the settings file).

## Appearance and graphics

* The default theme is dark on every system; Settings offers Dark, Light and Follow the system. Icons take their colours from the
  theme (`icons::set_light`). The viewport itself stays dark in both themes.
* The status bar shows a small "software drawing" note when the picture is drawn by a software adapter (tooltip explains it).

## Text and feedback

* UI texts are English in the code (the English text is the translation key); other languages live in `assets/lang/<code>.txt`. Messages say what went wrong and that the model was not changed.
* Shortcuts are shown in brackets after the tool name and on the card.
* Errors appear in the status bar in red; the document stays unchanged when an operation fails.
* The status bar always shows the version and build hash on the right.

## Colours in the viewport

* Hover: amber tint. Selection: blue tint. Sketch curves: yellow. Sketch region fill: light blue. Edges: thick amber (hover) or blue (selected).
* View icons (Top, Front, Right, Isometric) show the same cube with the face they look at filled in the accent colour; Round and
  Chamfer show the same corner with a round or a straight cut, and a radius mark or distance ticks.
* Numeric fields accept a decimal point and a decimal comma in every language.
* The soft error tone plays only when an operation fails and an error is shown (not on Esc cancelling); it can be turned off in Settings.

## Measuring and long calculations

* The Measure tool uses a yellow dimension line with the value on a dark label, and a salmon arc for angles; the axes distance is a dashed light-blue line.
  Hovered points get a green ring. Results live in a movable panel; a click on a value copies it.
* A calculation longer than 0.3 s shows a small panel at the top of the view (spinner, seconds, Cancel, "(Esc)"); shorter ones show nothing.
* Left column: Round and Chamfer sit side by side (icons) so the column fits a window 720 px high. Top bar icons are 27 px in 38 x 34 px buttons.

## Availability of buttons: traffic light

A button has three states: **chosen** (blue background, as before), **available** (normal background, white text, full-colour icon, the shortcut
letter in muted green) and **unavailable** (the background changes as it did when the button was greyed out, the text stays white and readable, the icon is
dimmed, the shortcut letter is muted red). A button without a visible shortcut letter gets a dot in the same corner: a filled green one when available,
a red ring when not (so the shape is a second cue next to the colour). In the left column the letter in the brackets, "Sweep (W)", is coloured.
Buttons that are always available (views, files, settings, About) have no indication. The tooltip with the reason stays.

* Green and red differ in brightness (a test checks the contrast ratio in both themes) and the dimmed icon is a cue that does not depend on colour.
* The traffic light is the only way (there is no greyed-out variant).
* The main button is Sketch: larger, violet (not the blue of a chosen tool). While sketching it becomes "Finish sketch" with a check mark; a click or K finishes.
* An empty document shows a quiet "Start with a sketch (K)" in the middle of the view until the first action.

## Turning the view

Turning to a sketch plane, back after the sketch, the standard views, Fit all and the plan view (V) are animated: about 0.3 to 0.5 s (never over 1 s) with an
eased start and stop, along the shorter way; the Z axis stays up, so the picture is never upside down. A horizontal plane keeps the nearest right-angled turn
about Z. The zoom frames the outline of the face and the shapes already drawn on the plane; with nothing there the scale stays. A click, a drag or the wheel
interrupts the animation. Settings > "Turn the view square to the sketch automatically" (default on) switches the turn to a sketch (and back) off.

## Highlight and selection

* The highlight shows exactly what the tool acts on. Move and Combine tint the **whole body** (hover amber; selected blue; Combine target cyan, tools magenta), never one face.
* Select: a click takes a face as before, a double click takes the whole body (the Selection panel then shows the body: volume, mass, material); a click on a body in the Document panel does the same.
* Smooth edges (the seams between faces that continue each other: the turns of a spring, the seam of a cylinder) are drawn thin and faint (22 % of the edge colour); sharp edges as before. They can still be picked and measured.
* A face shows its area once ("Area"). When a curve and a body edge lie in the same place the curve is picked first; clicking the same place again takes the next candidate.
* The view turned to a sketch plane never zooms in closer than a window 20 mm across.

## Presentation mode (a help for pictures of the window)

With `ROLIDIUM_PRESENTATION=1` the status bar leaves out the label of software drawing and the name of the graphics card, so that pictures of the window for the web show nothing about how they were drawn; nothing else changes (behaviour, calculations, the diagnostics and the log still say how the picture is really drawn), and there is no switch in Settings.

## Links, patterns, mirrors and groups

* Pattern (`T`) and Mirror (`B`) are icon buttons next to Fill and Join ends; their panel floats over the view like the others (`docks.panel`, kind `link`). Source bodies are outlined in magenta,
  the target body of "add" and "cut" in cyan; the preview is translucent blue, pieces that overlap each other or lie outside the target are red, with a message in the panel.
* The handle of the spacing is an orange disc at the first copy; dragging snaps to whole millimetres, Shift is free.
* In the right column, **Links** come between Bodies and Sketches (an eye shows or hides the bodies of the link, a warning sign marks a failed recalculation, a click opens the panel);
  bodies made by a link have a chain mark in the list. **Groups** are a tree with collapse arrows; bodies and groups are dragged onto a group (while dragging, a row "Out of every group" appears).
* A hand edit of a body made by a link opens a question (remove the link and edit / cancel). Every change of a link is one step of Undo.
